name: Layton
description: The one the whole region asks for by name. Apple and lavender over a vanilla that never quite finishes.

name: Layton Exclusif
description: Layton with the lights down: the same apple opening, resolved into incense and sandalwood instead of sugar.

name: Pegasus
description: Almond and heliotrope done without a trace of dessert. The quietest way to be noticed.

name: Althair
description: Vanilla with its sleeves rolled up — warm, powdery, and far more masculine than it reads on paper.

name: Herod
description: Sweet tobacco and cinnamon. The cold-weather bottle people buy in Nairobi for the Nakuru evenings.

name: Delina
description: The modern rose: rhubarb and lychee keeping it bright, cashmeran keeping it close to the skin all day.

name: Delina Exclusif
description: Delina with the volume up and the sugar down. Rose, still, but wearing a heavier coat.

name: Valaya
description: Clean laundry made expensive. White musk and orange blossom, nothing shouting, everything noticed.

name: Valaya Exclusif
description: The same soft musk, richer in the base. For the evening version of the same day.

name: Carlisle
description: Spiced apple over amber — Layton's older cousin, drier and considerably more serious.

name: Cassili
description: Pear and jasmine, lifted and kept there. The daytime bottle in a house known for evenings.

name: Godolphin
description: Saffron and leather with the oud kept on a short leash. A suit, not a statement.

name: Habdan
description: The house's Arabian register: rose and incense folded into oud, built for a climate that eats soft fragrance.

name: Sedley
description: Cold mint and vetiver. The answer when someone says they want something for Mombasa.

name: Oajan
description: Honeyed pear over oud — the sweet end of the Arabian shelf, and the easiest of them to wear.

name: Oriana
description: Guava and blackcurrant, unapologetically fruity, held together by a musk that keeps it from being a cordial.

name: Safanad
description: Iris done warm instead of cold — pear and orange blossom over a powdery sandalwood.

name: Meliora
description: Honey and pear kept just this side of edible. Soft, close, and difficult to put down.

name: Palatine
description: White flowers at full volume, with a vanilla base doing the talking after the first hour.

name: Perseus
description: Clean and green at the top, dry wood underneath. The least sweet thing the house makes.

name: Kalan
description: Rum and cinnamon over vanilla — the house at its most convivial.

name: Percival
description: Lavender kept crisp instead of soapy, over ambergris. Office-safe without being invisible.

name: Haltane
description: Juniper and vetiver, dry as a gin and twice as persistent. The newest face of the house.

name: Amore Caffe
description: Espresso and hazelnut. Ridiculous on paper, extremely effective on skin.

name: Aoud Orchid
description: Orchid and saffron over oud. Floral on the way in, Arabian on the way out.

name: Cedrat Boise
description: Lemon over leather and oud — loud, long, and built for heat. Twelve hours is normal.

name: Cosmic Pepper
description: Pepper and amber, dry and slightly metallic. Among the house's more grown-up compositions.

name: French Riviera
description: The lighter read of the same idea: sea spray, citrus, and a musk that holds it down.

name: Hindu Kush
description: Green, resinous and faintly smoky. The oddest thing on the shelf and a cult object for it.

name: Instant Crush
description: Red berries and vanilla, close to the skin and slow to leave.

name: Intense French Riviera
description: Salt air and citrus with Mancera's usual refusal to fade. Coastal without being a cliché.

name: Melody of the Sun
description: Tropical fruit without the suncream accord. Bright, sweet, and very hard to dislike.

name: Roses Greedy
description: Rose dipped in caramel. Sweeter than Roses Vanille and entirely unbothered about it.

name: Roses Vanille
description: Rose and vanilla with a coconut seam running through it. The best-selling bottle in the house, and it earns it.

name: Sicily
description: Lemon groves, fig leaf, and enough musk to survive a Nairobi afternoon.

name: Tonka Cola
description: A cola top note that has no business working, over tonka that makes it respectable.

name: Xplicit Vanilla
description: Vanilla as the whole argument. No fruit, no flowers, no apology.

name: Black Aoud
description: The bottle that taught a generation what oud smells like. Rose, smoke and medicine, in that order.

name: Starry Nights
description: Saffron and oud softened by vanilla — the gentlest way into the house's Aoud line.

name: Intense Starry Nights
description: Starry Nights with the oud pushed forward and the vanilla pulled back.

name: Arabians Tonka
description: Tonka and saffron over oud. Sweet, dense, and the most-reordered Montale after Black Aoud.

name: Arabians
description: Oud without the sugar — drier and more austere than anything else on this shelf.

name: Chocolate Greedy
description: Cocoa and orange peel. Easily the most literal fragrance in the room, and it still sells out.

name: Roses Musk
description: Rose and white musk, nothing else in the way. The cleanest rose the house makes.

name: Crazy in Love
description: Raspberry and praline over a rose. Young, loud, and extremely popular with its audience.

name: Intense Cafe Ristretto
description: Rose and espresso — the house's most copied idea, in its most concentrated form.

name: Sensual Instinct
description: Leather and saffron over oud, with just enough vanilla to keep it civil.

name: Oudyssee
description: Incense and cardamom folded into oud. Closer to a mosque than a boutique, and better for it.

name: Wood & Spices
description: Dry spice and cedar. The house's quietest bottle and the one that works at a desk.
